boundary_text: Lincoln Square is Chicago community area 4: Montrose Ave to the south, Ravenswood Ave and the Metra tracks to the east, Bryn Mawr and Peterson Aves to the north, and the North Branch of the Chicago River to the west. It's a mostly residential North Side area of flats, houses and small apartment buildings, with shops along Lincoln, Lawrence and Western and a strip of old factory buildings beside the tracks.

buildings.title: Two-flat or three-flat
buildings.where: Winnemac Park, Bowmanville, Ravenswood Gardens and west of Western
buildings.changes: One building service split between units, with a meter and panel for each unit in the basement. Laundry, kitchens and air conditioning outgrow the old 100-amp service, so an upgrade replaces the whole meter bank.

buildings.title: Older single-family house
buildings.where: Ravenswood Gardens, the side streets off Lincoln Ave and west of Western
buildings.changes: Rear additions, decks and basement remodels that go under a full building permit with plans, and older wiring that turns up once walls are opened.

buildings.title: Larger apartment building
buildings.where: Ravenswood along Wolcott, and near Lincoln Ave and Leavitt
buildings.changes: Buildings with 14 to 26 meters need a large main service, a meter bank and a panel for every unit, planned with ComEd and the owner so tenants lose power for as short a time as possible.

buildings.changes: Tenant finish-outs with plans, fire alarm systems for uses such as daycares, and new services in older commercial buildings. Exterior work on a landmarked facade is reviewed by the City's landmarks staff.

scope_lede: The same job on paper can cost very differently in a three-flat with a meter for every unit, an older house with a garage off the alley and an apartment building with 26 meters. These are the things that change it, and most are settled at the walkthrough.
scope_rows: Many older flats and houses here still have 100-amp services. An EV charger, central air or a kitchen remodel can mean a 200-amp service first.
In a two- or three-flat, an upgrade usually replaces a bank of meters and a panel for each unit, not one panel.
ComEd won't upgrade the service drop until the riser and weatherhead meet its rules, and its appointment sets the cut-over date.
Many lots have a garage off the alley. A charger or coach-house feed can mean trenching and underground conduit from the house.
Fuse boxes, cloth-covered wire and earlier owners' do-it-yourself work turn up in older houses and flats, and opening walls changes the scope.
These go under a full building permit with plans, not the Express Permit Program, and the electrical follows the architect's drawings and the builder's schedule.
A building with 15 to 26 meters needs a new main service, a meter bank and a panel per unit, scheduled with the owner around tenants.
Lincoln Ave shopfronts need tenant permits with plans, and work on a Chicago Landmark such as the Krause Music Store's facade is reviewed by the City's landmarks staff.
Parking near Lincoln Ave and the Brown Line stops is tight, which changes how materials and crews get in.
Shops and occupied buildings may need early or late work, and tenants in flats need notice before the power goes off. Agree the hours before the job is scheduled.
Service upgrades, new circuits and charger installs usually go through the City's Express Permit Program. 31 of our 52 Lincoln Square permits did.
hourly_answer: We quote by scope, not by the hour, because the hours on a Lincoln Square job depend on the factors below. Replacing a 100-amp service on a three-flat means three meters, three panels and a ComEd appointment, while adding one circuit in a house is a much smaller job. The written quote tells you the whole price before you agree to it.
choosing_building_why: A three-flat with a meter for each unit, an older house with a garage off the alley and an apartment building with 26 meters on Wolcott are three different jobs.

choosing_paperwork_why: Additions, decks and coach houses need a full City building permit with plans, and work on a Chicago Landmark such as the Krause Music Store's facade is reviewed by the City's landmarks staff.

Large commercial and institutional projects are for the big commercial firms, and we'll tell you so.

honest_context: We're a north-side shop at 5766 N Lincoln Ave in West Ridge, a few minutes up Lincoln Ave from Lincoln Square. Most of our roughly 1,200 City of Chicago permits since 2012 are in Wards 1, 32, 26, 47 and 27, and the 47th covers a large part of Lincoln Square. Our permits here, about 50 since 2014, are mostly residential: service upgrades for flats and houses, new circuits, and the electrical for additions and new three-unit buildings.

In the 24 months to October 2026, about 15 Lincoln Square permits named us, and only three of the electrical contractors on the area's permits were named more often. The rest of the record is spread across about 200 contractors, and solar appears on about 55 of the electrical permits, none of them ours.

faq: Can you upgrade the service on my Lincoln Square two- or three-flat?

Yes. It's the most common job in our Lincoln Square record: a 100-amp service replaced with a 200-amp service and a meter and panel for each unit, on blocks such as W Summerdale, W Farragut, N Hamilton and N California. We pull the City permit and coordinate the ComEd work.
Can you wire a new coach house or garage in Lincoln Square?

Yes. Our record includes a 2026 permit for a new three-car garage with a coach house under the City's ADU ordinance on the 2200 block of W Giddings St. Whether your lot can take a coach house is a zoning question for the City; once it can, we design the feed from the house, often underground, and handle the electrical permit.
Can you install an EV charger in my garage off the alley?

Yes. In 2025 we added garage charger circuits on the 2600 block of W Wilson and the 1900 block of W Summerdale, both on existing 200-amp services. If your service is smaller, the upgrade usually comes first, and a detached garage can need a trench and new conduit.
Do you work on larger apartment buildings in Lincoln Square?

Yes. In 2024 we replaced a 400-amp service with a 1,200-amp service, 26 meters and 26 panels in a building on the 4800 block of N Wolcott, and in 2014 we installed 1,200-amp services with 15 and 14 meters on the 4500 block of N Leavitt. We plan the cut-over with the owner and ComEd.
Do I need landmark approval for electrical work on Lincoln Ave?

Only on a designated Chicago Landmark. In Lincoln Square those are the Krause Music Store's facade on the 4600 block of N Lincoln Ave and the Rosehill Cemetery entrance, and permit work on them is reviewed by the City's landmarks staff. Most shopfronts on Lincoln Ave need an ordinary City permit.
Which Lincoln Square ZIP codes do you cover?
All of them: 60625 for most of the area, 60640 on the Ravenswood side, and 60659 and 60660 north of Bryn Mawr, along with every other Chicago neighbourhood.
